questions.question: Identify the incorrect sentence.

options.text: Beautiful furnitures made the house elegant.
How much money do you want?
He is a very good friend of mine.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Beautiful furnitures made the house elegant .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"furniture"** is an uncountable noun in English.
 
• Uncountable nouns do not have a plural form and are always treated as singular. Therefore, the word **"furnitures"** is incorrect.
 
• The correct sentence should use the singular form **"furniture"**, not its plural.
 
• Corrected sentence: **Beautiful furniture made the house elegant.**

Correct sentence: *Beautiful furniture made the house elegant*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uncountable nouns:**
 
 
• **Definition:** Nouns that cannot be counted and are treated as singular.
 
• **Examples:** furniture, information, water, advice, etc.
 
• **Usage:** Use singular verbs and quantifiers like "some," "a lot of," or "a piece of" for uncountable nouns.
 
 
 
• **Countable nouns:**
 
 
• **Definition:** Nouns that can be counted and have both singular and plural forms.
 
• **Examples:** chair, book, apple, etc.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
**Fill in the blank with the most appropriate preposition:**

__
 
• The phrase **"in accordance with"** is a standard expression used to indicate that something complies with or agrees with rules, laws, or standards.

• Other options such as "by," "to," or "under" do not fit the collocation or context of this sentence.

Correct sentence: *The policy was implemented **in accordance with** international standards*.

• Examples of usage:
 
 
• The company operates **in accordance with** environmental regulations.
 
• All procedures were conducted **in accordance with** the law.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

__
 
• The given sentence indicates a condition where two possible outcomes are mentioned: she completes the registration or she won’t be allowed to participate.
 
• The conjunction **"or else"** is used to specify the consequences of not fulfilling the condition.
 
• Other options like **"unless," "and,"** or **"since"** do not fit the context of providing a consequence.

Correct sentence: *She must complete the registration by Friday, **or else** she won’t be allowed to participate.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of Conjunctions:**

 
 
• **Or else:** Used to indicate the consequence of an action. (e.g., Finish your homework, or else you won’t be allowed to play.)
 
• **Unless:** Indicates an exception. (e.g., You can’t go out unless you finish your work.)
 
• **And:** Connects two ideas or actions. (e.g., She read the book and wrote a review.)
 
• **Since:** Indicates a reason or time. (e.g., Since it was raining, we stayed indoors.)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: **Euphemism**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Directness .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **Euphemism** refers to a polite or mild word or expression used to refer to something unpleasant or embarrassing, often to soften the impact.
 
• An antonym for **Euphemism** would be a term that conveys bluntness or straightforwardness, without softening the expression.
 
• **Directness**, as an antonym, matches this idea as it involves being straightforward, candid, or frank, without using softer or gentler language.

• **Substitute:** Refers to replacing one thing with another, which is unrelated to the antonym of Euphemism.
 
• **Vagueness:** Refers to a lack of clarity or precision, which is not directly opposite to Euphemism.

questions.question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

The mother said to the child, "Don't touch the hot iron."

options.text: The mother warned the child not to touch the hot iron.
The mother told the child not to touched the hot iron.
The mother warned the child not to be touching the hot iron.
The mother requested the child never to touching the hot iron.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. The mother warned the child not to touch the hot iron.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is a direct speech in the form of an imperative sentence with a negative command: **"Don't touch the hot iron."**
 
• When converting such sentences into indirect speech, we use the reporting verb **"warned"** to indicate caution.
 
• The word **"not"** is used before the verb to maintain the negative meaning.
 
• The infinitive form of the verb (**"to touch"**) is used in the indirect narration.

Correct sentence: *The mother warned the child not to touch the hot iron.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Incorrect Options:**
 
 
• **Option 2:** "The mother told the child not to touched the hot iron." 
 
Grammatically incorrect because "touched" is the past tense, whereas the infinitive "to touch" should have been used.
 
• **Option 3:** "The mother warned the child not to be touching the hot iron." 
 
Incorrect because "not to be touching" is not a suitable structure in indirect speech.
 
• **Option 4:** "The mother requested the child never to touching the hot iron." 
 
Incorrect because "requested" does not convey the warning tone, and "to touching" is grammatically wrong.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
**Change the following sentence into the Active form.**

The intricate design will have been conceived by a team of engineers.

options.text: A team of engineers will conceive the intricate design.
The intricate design will conceive a team of engineers.
A team of engineers will have conceived the intricate design.
The intricate design has been conceived by a team of engineers.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. A team of engineers will have conceived the intricate design .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence given is in the **passive voice**. The passive structure is: **"Object + will have been + past participle + by + subject."**
 
• To convert the sentence into the **active voice**, the subject and object swap places, and the verb form changes accordingly.
 
• The correct active voice structure would be: **"Subject + will have + past participle + object."**

Correct sentence: *A team of engineers will have conceived the intricate design.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Active Voice:** The subject performs the action expressed by the verb.
 
 
• **Example:** The cat chased the mouse.
 
 
 
• **Passive Voice:** The subject receives the action expressed by the verb.
 
 
• **Example:** The mouse was chased by the cat.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.**

The young artist confidently announced that she could paint a masterpiece if she were given enough time.

options.text: The young artist announced, "I can paint a masterpiece if I am given enough time."
The young artist said, "She could paint a masterpiece if she was given enough time."
The young artist announced, "I could paint a masterpiece if I were given enough time."
The young artist said, "I can paint a masterpiece if I were given enough time."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. The young artist announced, "I can paint a masterpiece if I am given enough time." .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **indirect speech**, where the young artist reported her ability to paint a masterpiece under a certain condition.
 
• To convert it into the **direct speech**, the reporting verb remains in the **past tense** ("announced"), but the exact words of the speaker need to be quoted.
 
• When reporting in the **direct voice**, the speaker's original words are retained, and the pronouns are adjusted accordingly.
 
• The original sentence in **direct speech** would be: "I can paint a masterpiece if I am given enough time."

Correct sentence: *The young artist announced, "I can paint a masterpiece if I am given enough time."*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Difference between direct and indirect speech**:

 
 
• **Direct Speech:** The exact words of the speaker are quoted within quotation marks. Example: She said, "I am happy."
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The speaker's words are paraphrased without quotation marks. Example: She said that she was happy.
 
 
 
• **Tense Changes in Reported Speech**:
 
 
• If the reporting verb is in the past tense, the tenses of the direct speech are usually shifted back in indirect speech.
 
• For example, "I can" becomes "she could" in indirect speech.
 
• However, for this question, the sentence is already provided in indirect speech, and we are converting it back to direct speech.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:**

The diligent worker performs his tasks with meticulous care every single day.

options.text: His tasks are performed with meticulous care by the diligent worker every single day.
His tasks were performed with meticulous care by the diligent worker every single day.
His tasks are being performed with meticulous care by the diligent worker every single day.
The diligent worker is performed with meticulous care by his tasks every single day.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. His tasks are performed with meticulous care by the diligent worker every single day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **active voice**, where the subject “the diligent worker” performs the action (performs his tasks).
 
• To convert this to the **passive voice**, the object of the active sentence “his tasks” becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The tense of the original sentence is **present simple**, so the passive form must use “are performed.”
 
• The correct structure is: **Object + is/are + past participle + by + subject.**

Correct sentence: *His tasks are performed with meticulous care by the diligent worker every single day.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Simple Passive Structure:** Object + is/are + past participle.
 
• **Example:** The book is read by many people.
 
• **Usage:** Used to emphasize the action or the object of the action rather than the doer.

questions.question:
"plants that demand minimal vigilance have become almost axiomatic for those seeking verdant comfort within their domiciles."

Convert the sentence into Interrogative sentence.

options.text: plants that demand minimal vigilance have not become almost axiomatic for those seeking verdant comfort within their domiciles?
Is plants that demand minimal vigilance have become almost axiomatic for those seeking verdant comfort within their domiciles?
Why plants that demand minimal vigilance have become almost axiomatic for those seeking verdant comfort within their domiciles?
Have plants that demand minimal vigilance become almost axiomatic for those seeking verdant comfort within their domiciles?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Interrogative Transformation:** To convert an assertive sentence into an interrogative one, we typically move the auxiliary verb to the beginning of the sentence. In the phrase "plants... **have become**," the auxiliary verb is **"have"**.
 
• **Correct Structure:** Option 4 correctly places **"Have"** at the start, followed by the subject ("plants that demand minimal vigilance") and the past participle ("become"), ending with a question mark.
 
• **Analysis of Incorrect Options:** 
 
 
• **Option 1:** Simply adds a question mark to a negative statement without correct inversion.
 
• **Option 2:** Incorrectly uses "Is" with a plural subject and the auxiliary "have."
 
• **Option 3:** While it uses "Why," it does not invert the subject and auxiliary verb, which is necessary for a standard interrogative structure.
 
 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Axiomatic:** In this context, it means something that is self-evident or unquestionable; it has become a "given" for urban dwellers.
 
• **Verdant Comfort:** This refers to the lush, green aesthetic provided by indoor plants, which the passage suggests mitigates the "anxieties concomitant with horticulture".
 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:** Note that "plants" is a plural subject, hence the use of the plural auxiliary verb **"have"**.

• **Amelioration:** A formal term meaning the act of making something better or improving it. In this context, it refers to skin care or healing.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:**

P: The public park in the city was converted into a lively community centre with green areas and recreational facilities.

Q: It was a much-awaited project that united the community and had a friendly environment.

R: The park soon became a favourite destination for families, fitness buffs, and nature enthusiasts.

S: Volunteers and local businesses joined hands to donate resources such as plants, benches, and tools.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. P, S, Q, R.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The paragraph begins with sentence **P**, which introduces the idea of converting the park into a community center with green areas and recreational facilities. This sets the context for the rest of the passage.
 
• Sentence **S** logically follows as it describes the effort made by volunteers and local businesses to contribute resources for the transformation of the park.
 
• Sentence **Q** explains the significance of this project by mentioning how it united the community and provided a friendly environment.
 
• Finally, sentence **R** concludes the paragraph by describing the outcome — the park becoming a favorite destination for families, fitness enthusiasts, and nature lovers.

Correct paragraph: *The public park in the city was converted into a lively community centre with green areas and recreational facilities. Volunteers and local businesses joined hands to donate resources such as plants, benches, and tools. It was a much-awaited project that united the community and had a friendly environment. The park soon became a favourite destination for families, fitness buffs, and nature enthusiasts.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rearrangement tips:** Look for sentences that establish the context (introduction), provide supporting details, and conclude the passage. This logical sequence ensures the paragraph is meaningful and coherent.
 
• Pay attention to transitional words and logical connections between sentences to determine the correct order.

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs of homonyms can be used to fill in the blanks most suitably?

As his ____ ring slipped from his finger and sank into the pond, a curious ____ paddled over and, mistaking it for food, swallowed it whole.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. signet, cygnet .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence requires a pair of homonyms that fit appropriately into the context of the blanks.
 
• The first blank refers to a type of ring. The word "signet" (a type of ring) fits perfectly here.
 
• The second blank refers to a creature paddling over in the pond. The word "cygnet" (a young swan) is ideal here.
 
• Therefore, the pair "signet" and "cygnet" best completes the sentence.

Correct sentence: *As his **signet** ring slipped from his finger and sank into the pond, a curious **cygnet** paddled over and, mistaking it for food, swallowed it whole*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Homonyms** are words that sound the same or are spelled the same but have different meanings.
 
• In this question, the pair "signet" (a type of ring) and "cygnet" (a young swan) are homonyms that fit the context.
 
• Other options do not match the context of the sentence.
</ul

questions.question: What is the term for someone who believes in more than one God?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Polytheist .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term "Polytheist" refers to someone who believes in more than one God.
 
• "Monotheist" (Option 1) refers to someone who believes in only one God.
 
• "Atheist" (Option 2) refers to someone who does not believe in God or gods.
 
• "Agnostic" (Option 4) refers to someone who believes that the existence of God or gods is unknown or unknowable.

Correct sentence: *The term for someone who believes in more than one God is **Polytheist**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Polytheism:** The belief in or worship of multiple deities typically assembled into a pantheon of gods and goddesses.
 
• Examples of polytheistic religions include Hinduism, Ancient Greek religion, and Norse mythology.
</ul
